classification.difficultyReason: Apply the secant product rule symbolically, cancel equal external lengths, then subtract them from equal whole secants to justify equal internal segments.

spec.description: Two secants from P at the left, meeting the circle in order P–A–B and P–D–C. Matching double ticks mark PA=PD. Circle intersections are coordinate-derived.
spec.mathematics: PA×PB=PD×PC; PA=PD>0 gives PB=PC, so PB−PA=PC−PD.
spec.answerVisibility: Point names and the given equal-length ticks only; no proof or answer appears in the figure.

answer.short: The secant product rule gives $AP\times BP=DP\times CP$. Since $AP=DP$, $BP=CP$. Subtracting the equal external segments gives $AB=DC$.
answer.worked:
By the secant product rule,
$$AP\times BP=DP\times CP.$$
Since $AP=DP$ and these lengths are nonzero, $BP=CP$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}AB&=BP-AP\\&=CP-DP\\&=DC.\end{align*}$$
